(2) The individual leans forward, placing their forearms and head on the mat, and slowly begins to lift their hips and legs into the air. The camera remains static at an eye-level perspective, capturing the controlled movement as the person transitions into an inverted pose. They hold this posture steadily for a significant duration, showcasing balance and core strength. The natural daylight from the window provides even, bright lighting across the scene. (4) After holding the headstand, the person slowly lowers their legs back toward the floor with the same control used to ascend. They return to a kneeling position on the mat, resting briefly in a child's pose or similar restorative stance before the video ends.
